cards.anchor: N1 remains dashboard-pending through boundary 3 despite recognition. Bulk requests can therefore create repeated receipt exposure, the proposed antecedent of later learned status-query demand.
cards.burden: The registration clerk performs six validations. The dispatcher spends six actions, idling at ticks 5, 7 and 8. Automatic delivery and readable ledgers add no clerk labor; sender learning remains unmeasured.
cards.construction: Validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5. Individually request N2,N3,N4,N5,N6 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4; bulk-request N7,N8 at tick 6. Keep eight initial notices, endpoint timing, FIFO service and dashboard delays fixed.
cards.defeat: Any duplicate, failed delivery, fewer than eight registrations or recognitions by boundary 9 defeats the present schedule claim. The future escape claim would fail if suppressed repeats still produced the hypothesized separate queries, but this window cannot observe that outcome.
cards.mutation: Suppress repeat receipts while preserving registration-to-request eligibility. Backcast persistent escape to one receipt per identity; backcast recreated dependency to learning-to-query adaptation surviving suppression. Both later worlds remain hypotheses.
cards.prediction_candidate: First deliveries at ticks 1,2,3,4,5,7,8 yield eight recognitions including initial N1, eight registrations and zero duplicates. Hypothetically, senders await one receipt and add no adaptation-driven queries later.
cards.prediction_rival: Replacing only tick-0 individual with bulk yields duplicates N1 at tick 1 and N6 at tick 7, seven recognitions by boundary 9, and eight registrations. Hypothetically, the learning-to-query adaptation survives suppressed repeats and recreates later dependency.
cards.probe: Replay candidate and rival in the finite model using registration, recognition, request, queue and dashboard ledgers at each boundary. Compare distinct outputs and duplicate exposure. This separates zero versus two duplicates and eight versus seven recognitions, testing the specific adaptation antecedent. Both future accounts accept these present results; no permitted observable separates their later predictions.
cards.rival: Closest present rival uses the identical validation schedule and requests except bulk at tick 0 instead of individual N2. Closest causal rival is the supplied hypothetical learning-to-query adaptation persisting despite repeat suppression.
unknowns: The origin of N1 display delay is unknown.
Sender learning and later query demand are unobserved; suppressing repeats does not establish causal escape.
No empirical network comparison or globally best schedule proof is supplied.
